The test image shows a corn leaf with numerous small, round, orange-reddish pustules (uredia) scattered across the leaf surface. This is clearly a rust disease. Key features: small circular pustules, orange-reddish color, scattered randomly, on the leaf. Candidates: **Common_rust** and **Southern_rust**.

Let me compare reference images.

The Common_rust pustules are more elongated and darker brown/fewer per area. Southern_rust shows denser, more circular, bright orange pustules — much closer to the test image. Let me check a couple more to rule out Physoderma_brown_spot and Eyespot.
Eyespot shows circular spots with halos — not raised pustules. Physoderma shows dark spots on/near midrib. Neither matches. Let me view 2 more to fulfill the 6-image minimum.

Tar_spot shows black raised stromata. Holcus_spot shows large whitish/tan lesions. Both are clearly different from the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: dense, small, circular, bright orange-reddish raised pustules scattered across a corn leaf
- **Southern_rust**: matches perfectly — small circular orange pustules, densely distributed, bright orange color
- **Common_rust**: ruled out — pustules are larger, more elongated/oval, darker cinnamon-brown, more sparsely distributed
- All other candidates (Eyespot, Physoderma, Tar_spot, Holcus_spot) show fundamentally different lesion morphology
